audit.whatIsWrong: The entry repeatedly says to punish Riven's cooldowns but never names one, and the only cooldown claim it does make is backwards: late says 'Her W stun cooldown is long at this stage'.
audit.why: Ki Burst is 11/10/9/8/7 — by the time the entry calls it 'long' it is 7 seconds, the shortest it will ever be. The cooldown that actually decides this matchup is Broken Wings: 13 seconds flat at every rank, with all three casts sharing it. That is the one number a Tahm Kench needs, because a Riven who has spent her chain has only Valor to move with and cannot escape a 900-range Tongue Lash.
audit.corrected: Broken Wings is 13s at every rank and never gets shorter; count the three casts and commit on the empty chain. Ki Burst is 7s at rank 5, so it is not worth waiting out.
sources: champ-data/_kits/riven.json (Q Broken Wings cd 13, W Ki Burst 11/10/9/8/7, E Valor 10/9/8/7/6)

audit.whatIsWrong: Wind Slash is described as a threshold execute in three places: 'respect Wind Slash's execute threshold', 'Wind Slash executes below a health threshold', 'the execute reads your actual current HP', with the invented instruction 'Play at a comfortable HP buffer above 30%'.
audit.why: Wind Slash is not a threshold execute — its damage scales with the target's missing health, increasing continuously rather than switching on below a line. The entry's underlying insight is genuinely good and worth keeping: grey health is not current health, so a Tahm Kench sitting on a fat unconverted grey bar is at low current HP and is exactly the target Wind Slash punishes hardest. But '30%' is a number nobody can act on because it does not exist, and a player who believes there is a safe line above it will take the fight that kills him.
audit.corrected: Wind Slash scales with your missing health, with no threshold. Convert grey health with Thick Skin before she ults rather than banking damage through it.

audit.whatIsWrong: early says that at level 3 Riven 'can interrupt your Devour cast itself, which is her kill tool — she W-stuns you mid-swallow, you lose the lockdown'.
audit.why: Devour is Tahm Kench's ultimate. He does not have it at level 3. The paragraph covers levels 1 to 3 and describes Riven countering an ability that will not exist for another three levels. Separately, whether Ki Burst actually interrupts a Devour cast is not something the kit data settles, so the claim should not be reintroduced later either.
audit.corrected: At level 3 Ki Burst on 11 seconds is her kill tool outright, not an answer to Devour — you have no Devour until 6.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[0] claims Riven can 'cancel Tongue Lash by being inside its dead zone'.
audit.why: Tongue Lash is a 900-range skillshot with no minimum range documented anywhere in the kit data. There is no dead zone to stand in, and a player told to fear one will misplay spacing in both directions. What Broken Wings actually gives her is three 275-unit dashes on a single cooldown to close and to juke the skillshot.
audit.corrected: Broken Wings closes 275 units a cast, three casts on one 13s cooldown — that is how she gets on top of you, not a dead zone.

audit.whatIsWrong: Tahm Kench's W is called 'Abyssal Voyage' in mid and late, and in late it is the tool that lets you 'arrive in teamfights first'.
audit.why: The live W is Abyssal Dive: 1000-1200 range with a knockup, on 21/20/19/18/17, from level 2. It crosses a lane, not a map, and it does not get you anywhere first.

The displacement race flagged in _missing-interactions.json is already handled in substance — the entry warns about the Q3 knockup breaking your commit, and Abyssal Dive's own knockup is the mirror of it. No edit needed; adding a line restating it would be filler.

edits.after: Riven's Blade of the Exile doubles her burst window; Wind Slash scales with your missing health, so an unconverted grey-health bar makes it hit hardest.

edits.after: Bait out all three Broken Wings casts — that is a full 13 seconds with no gap-closer — then stun and Devour her

edits.after: Open with Broken Wings — three 275-unit dashes on one cooldown — to close and juke your Q

edits.after: Animation-cancel Q3 into Wind Slash while your grey health is still unconverted, so the missing-health scaling is at its maximum

edits.after: Blade of the Exile at level 6 doubles her burst and Wind Slash scales off your missing health — the fatter your unconverted grey bar, the harder it lands, so shield before she ults.

edits.before: At level 1 this is a neutral feeling push — your Tongue Lash range can tap her for the first Acquired Taste stack but she has no gap-closer yet, so neither of you can force a real trade. The moment she hits level 2 she has Q dash and the calculus flips: she will Q-Q-Q into you and animation-cancel her third Q knockup before you can stagger a stun, so do not trade into her three-Q window at level 2. At level 3 she adds W stun and can interrupt your Devour cast itself, which is her kill tool — she W-stuns you mid-swallow, you lose the lockdown and take the full combo. Play the level 2 and 3 phases at the edge of Tongue Lash range, land free pokes to build stacks, and accept that you are not winning the trade if she chooses to all-in; activate Thick Skin to shield her burst and let grey health tick back when she disengages.
edits.after: At level 1 this is a neutral feeling push — your Tongue Lash range can tap her for the first Acquired Taste stack but she has no gap-closer yet, so neither of you can force a real trade. The moment she hits level 2 she has Broken Wings and the calculus flips: three 275-unit dashes sharing one 13-second cooldown, and she animation-cancels the third knockup before you can stagger a stun, so do not trade into that window. At level 3 she adds Ki Burst on 11 seconds, and that is her kill tool outright — not an answer to Devour, which you do not have until 6. Play levels 2 and 3 at the edge of Tongue Lash range, land free pokes to build stacks, and accept that you are not winning a trade she chooses; activate Thick Skin to shield her burst and let grey health tick back when she disengages.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 is a standoff — she can dash in and out of your stun range faster than you can land three stacks, and you have no ultimate yet to threaten a macro escape, so respect her aggression and fish for stack-fishing Tongue Lash pokes while she is resetting the wave. At level 6 her Blade of the Exile is the sharpest danger point: Wind Slash executes below a health threshold that your grey health does NOT protect against — the execute reads your actual current HP, not grey health. Play at a comfortable HP buffer above 30% and do not let her force the exchange after an all-in where your grey health has not converted yet. Your Abyssal Voyage at 6 does not help you win the duel but it does give you a safety valve — if she burns E dash and W stun on a botched engage, that is the one window to flash-stun-Devour her before she rebuilds her shield.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 is a standoff — she dashes in and out of your stun range faster than you land three stacks, so fish Tongue Lash pokes from max range while she resets the wave and count her casts instead. Broken Wings is 13 seconds at every rank and all three dashes share it: once the chain is spent she has only Valor to move with, and that is your window. At level 6 Blade of the Exile is the sharpest danger point: Wind Slash scales with your missing health, and grey health is not current health — a full grey bar means you are precisely the target it hits hardest, so convert with Thick Skin before she ults rather than banking through it. Abyssal Dive will not win you the duel, but if she botches an engage into an empty chain, that is the window to dive, stun and Devour her.

edits.before: Past first item your grey-health healing finally outruns her burst cycle in extended fights, and the Tongue Lash stun into Devour combo becomes a genuine teamfight removal tool — she is the squishiest melee bruiser on the map and being swallowed for two seconds ends her entire engage. At 2+ items she effectively cannot kill you in a straight fight; focus on using Abyssal Voyage to arrive in teamfights first, tank the frontline, and save Devour for when she flashes into your backline so you yank her out and give your carries free hits. Her W stun cooldown is long at this stage — bait it with a fake Devour attempt, then swallow her for real on the follow-up.
edits.after: Past first item your grey-health healing finally outruns her burst cycle in extended fights, and the Tongue Lash stun into Devour combo becomes a genuine teamfight removal tool — she is the squishiest melee bruiser on the map and being swallowed for two seconds ends her entire engage. At 2+ items she effectively cannot kill you in a straight fight; use Abyssal Dive to cross the last 1200 units into the frontline, and save Devour for when she jumps your backline so you yank her out and give your carries free hits. Do not wait out Ki Burst — it is 7 seconds at rank 5. Broken Wings, still 13, is the one worth counting.

edits.before: - Riven Ki Burst: matchup-defining — Her engage CC. Q-stun/dodge it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Riven Broken Wings: 13s at every rank, all three dashes share it — count the chain, commit on empty. - Ki Burst is 7s at rank 5, do not wait on it. - Devour: kill windows only, never chip.

edits.before: Devour deletes him from the fight — or you from his. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Riven's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Devour deletes her from a fight. But Wind Slash scales off your missing health — convert grey health before she ults.

notes: Riven is the lowest win rate of my nine that is still close (49.67% over 765 games) and the entry had two claims that would actively get a player killed: an invented 30% Wind Slash safety threshold, and a level-3 paragraph built around Riven countering Devour three levels before Tahm Kench learns it. Both fixed. I did not touch the assertion that Ki Burst interrupts a Devour cast where it appears as a general late-game idea, because the kit data does not settle cast-interrupt behaviour and needsResearch is empty by design — it is unverified, not confirmed false.
